newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares tumbled on Thursday, undermined at the opening by a weak Wall Street close, which prompted a bout of profit-taking on a blue-chip AEX index which has recently raced to consecutive record highs.
The main AEX index ended down 10.66 points, or 1.14 percent, at 924.71. But the mid-cap AMX index closed 4.63 higher at 1,406.55 as several medium-sized companies put on hefty gains.

Amid the majors, Royal Dutch lost 2.60 guilders to 107.30 and banking group ING fell 2.40 to 103.00 guilders following huge gains notched up on the back of its $2.2 billion purchase of U.S. insurer Equitable of Iowa on Tuesday.
Philips also erased some its recent gains, shedding 3.70 to end at 144.10 guilders.
The Dutch AEX index had risen 44 percent through 1997 until yesterday. But as investors took profits on leading Dutch stocks, they seemed less willing to do so on medium-sized firms.
Among the stocks to defy the general weaker trend were tank storage and shipping group Pakhoed NV and semiconductor equipment maker ASM Lithography.
Pakhoed ended up 5.90 guilders to 76.40 in the wake of its announcement late on Wednesday that first half profit rose 75 percent and that it was upgrading its full year forecast.
ASM Lithography gained 7.80 to 134.60 guilders on news it had won an $150 million order from Micron Technology, one of the world's largest makers of computer memory chips.
A central bank decision to raise its special advances rate by 10 basis points to 3.00 percent had no impact on the market.
But dealers remained generally bullish on the main AEX index despite the sharp drop today.
SNS Securities said in a research note that any retreat to lower levels from the would create opportunities for investors to get into the market.
